newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia cuts foreign aid budget.
newsitem.headline: Australia cuts foreign aid budget.

text.p: The Australian government on Tuesday slashed foreign aid as part of widespread cuts aimed at reining in its budget deficit.
Total foreign aid has been cut by 8.5 percent in real terms to A$1.32 billion (US$1.03 billion) in the fiscal year from July from A$1.41 billion in 1996/97, budget documents showed.
This compares with a 1.4 percent real cut to total government spending in the Liberal-National coalition government's second budget.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said the reduction was modest in view of the government's efforts to wipe out the deficit, projected at A$3.853 billion when windfall items such as asset sales are excluded.

"Given the need for fiscal restraint, this outcome highlights the government's strong commitment to overseas aid and is a true reflection of a desire by the vast majority of Australians to assist the world's poor," he said in the budget papers.

As part of general cuts in the budget of the Foreign Affairs and Trade Department, Canberra will close its diplomatic missions in Copenhagen and Nauru and streamline the collection of charges from companies using the trade agency, Austrade.
Most of the cuts in Canberra's foreign aid spending hits East Asia, particularly Indonesia, African nations and multilateral agencies.
The government is also transferring A$4 million from its aid programme to help fund the continuation of a limited service by Radio Australia, its international radio broadcaster.
The funding will help Radio Australia, recently threatened with closure, maintain foreign language services in Tok Pisin, Indonesian, Mandarin, Vietnamese and Khmer.
